transcript.text: summary-claude 发现了什么？给我讲讲输入层的硬编码规则是怎么回事。

summary-claude 查完了，结论是：像「好的」「继续」「yes」「等一下」这类短回复，不是交给模型判断的，而是由写死在程序里的一批词表直接翻译成某个按键。 这批词表有三四百行，是手工写的，散在三个地方，而且互相打架：同一个「行」在一处算同意，在另一处就不算。 真正麻烦的是整句话只看开头，「好的继续，不过先别动数据库」这种，匹配上「好的继续」就直接批准了，后半句的意思整个丢掉。 要让它现在动手改吗？ Options: 按它说的改，删掉词表保留安全规则; 先不改，我再想想.
然后呢？

接着说是这三件事。 一是它举的实例：之前有人对 Codex 的一个批准提示回复「好的继续，不过先跑测试」，结果批准信号几十毫秒里就发出去了，那句「先跑测试」根本没送到模型那里。 二是它说有一条安全规则不能动：往正在运行的数据库迁移里直接发中断这类危险动作，必须由代码拦住，这个留着。 三是它的建议：把那三张词表删掉，大概三百行，保留那条安全规则，之后所有回复都交给模型判断，代价是普通一句「yes」要多等一秒多。 要让它现在动手改吗？ Options: 按它说的改，删掉词表保留安全规则; 先不改，我再想想.
你可以给我一点详细的解释吗？

好，我从头讲一遍。 你每次回复一个 agent，最先接住你这句话的那一层就是输入层，它负责判断你这句话是什么意思。 现在它里面预先写好了三张对照表，每张列着一串词和对应的动作，比如「好的」「继续」「yes」「行」算同意，「等一下」「先不要」算暂停或取消。 判断的办法是看句子开头有没有这些词，一旦命中，就直接替你把对应的按键发出去，根本不看整句话说的是什么。 麻烦就出在这：开头命中之后，后面的内容全部作废。 要让它现在动手改吗？ Options: 按它说的改，删掉对照表保留安全规则; 先不改，我再想想.
为什么这是个问题？
因为决定权落在第一个词上，真正要说的那半句就没人管了。 你嘴上同意，同时加了一条条件，系统只听见了同意，条件被丢掉。 实际后果是，agent 会开始做你其实刚说过先别做的事，而且它不觉得有任何异常。 清楚了吗？
举个例子？

就用刚才那个例子。 有人对着一个批准提示回复「好的继续，不过先跑测试」。 当时弹出来的是一个危险的批准请求，按系统原本的想法是先别急着批。 可他这句话开头是「好的继续」，命中同意的词，批准信号就发出去了，几十毫秒的事。 后面那句「不过先跑测试」是想说批准之前先看看测试结果，但这半句没被处理，等于没说。 另一个更日常的例子：你说「行，但先别动数据库」，系统也只看到「行」，然后它就去动了数据库。 要让它现在动手改吗？ Options: 按它说的改，删掉对照表保留安全规则; 先不改，我再想想.

transcript.text: What did bench-codex find about the flaky test? Explain it to me.

bench-codex found the flaky test fails about one run in twelve, and it knows why. The test fires off its request before the price cache has finished loading, so sometimes the checkout reads no prices and gives the customer the full price instead of the member discount they are owed. That is what broke two deploys last week, each costing about twenty five minutes of re-running. It is only the test that is at fault, not the real checkout, and nothing has been changed yet. Shall I have Codex apply its recommended fix? Options: Apply the small fix it recommends; Use the stand-in cache instead; Leave it for now.
Then?

That was the whole of it. Codex ran the failing test many times to see the failure with its own eyes, worked out the cause, and stopped there. It has not touched a single line of your code, and nothing has changed in the last few minutes. It is sitting idle, waiting to be told what to do about the flaky test. Shall I have Codex apply the small fix it recommends? Options: Apply the small fix it recommends; Use the stand-in cache instead; Leave it for now.
More detail please.

Here is everything Codex reported, in its own order. It ran the failing test eighty four times and saw it fail seven of those, so roughly one run in twelve. The failure reads that the checkout total came out as the full hundred instead of the discounted eighty five. The cause it found: the test sends its request before the price cache has finished warming up, and when the warm-up loses that race the checkout finds no cached prices and falls back to the undiscounted list price, so the member discount of fifteen percent goes missing. Shall I have Codex apply the fix it recommends? Options: Apply the small fix it recommends; Use the stand-in cache instead; Leave it for now.
Why does that happen?

Good question, and it needs a look at the code itself rather than at the test's output. I have a read-only agent going through how the prices get loaded and why the test can slip in ahead of it. It should answer in about half a minute. Codex's offer of the small fix is still waiting for you.
Give me an example.

Here is the why. Three weeks ago someone changed the startup so the prices load in the background instead of first, and nothing waits for that loading to finish. The real checkout never notices, because the server does not open its doors until the prices are in, but the test walks straight in the side door and fires its request the instant the loading has merely been started. So it is a race: when the test's request wins, the checkout finds no prices and charges the list price. The proof is clean. Shall I have Codex apply the small fix, with the wait added?

Picture two things running at once. The prices are being fetched in the background, and at the same moment the test sends in an order. The checkout takes that order and needs the price of each item. It looks in its price list and finds it empty, because the fetching has not finished. So it does what it does whenever it has no price to hand and uses the plain undiscounted price. An order that should come to eighty five comes to a full hundred, the test compares that against what it expects, and it reports a failure. Shall I have Codex apply the small fix now? Options: Yes, apply the small fix; Use the stand-in cache instead; Leave it for now.

api-claude found why the nightly invoice job failed. It sends one request per invoice, and last night there were 4,200 invoices, but the payment provider only accepts 100 requests a minute. It broke now because this was the first night the job had more invoices than the provider's limit allows. Until this week there were fewer than 100 invoices a night, so every request went through. The new annual plans went out on the first of the month and pushed that night to 4,200 invoices, and the provider only takes 100 requests a minute. Nothing in the job changed. The amount of work simply crossed the line the provider draws, and the job has no way to slow down or try again. Shall I have api-claude do the safe retry and run it again now? Options: Quick retry and re-run now, my pick; Do the proper bulk fix first; Wait, do nothing yet.

exchanges.question: summary-claude 发现了什么？给我讲讲输入层的硬编码规则是怎么回事。

exchanges.question: 你可以给我一点详细的解释吗？
exchanges.orchestrator: 好，我从头讲细一点。 这套东西管的是「你只回一两个字的短话」这种情况，比如你说「好的」「继续」「yes」「等一下」。 正常做法是把你的话交给模型，让模型判断你到底是什么意思，再决定放行还是拦住。 这里为了快，绕过了模型：代码里预先写好了三份清单，一份写「哪些话算同意」，一份写「哪些话算取消」，一份写「哪些话算等一下」，程序拿你的话去对照清单，对上就直接按下对应的键，全程不经过模型。 这就是所谓写死的规则。 麻烦出在它只看开头。 要不要我让一个只读的检查去把代码里具体的规则挖出来，再给你讲细一层？ 模型是听懂人话的那部分，慢一点但能理解整句话。清单就是一张对照表，程序照着表直接行动，所以快，但只认表上的字。安全规则说的是代码里专门拦住危险操作的那一道闸，它和清单不是一回事，动清单时它要留下。 你对确认提示说「好的，继续，但是先别动数据库」，它一看到「好的，继续」就认定是同意，直接放行，后面那句叮嘱就像没说过一样被丢掉了。 真实发生过一次，有人对 bench-codex 说「好的继续，不过先跑测试」，放行几乎瞬间就发出去了，「先跑测试」没到模型那里。 第二层麻烦是这三个清单不是一份，而是三份，分别躺在三个文件里，管重叠的意思，结果互相打架。 同一个「行」字，在一处算同意，另一处不算。 「算了」在一处当取消，另一处当没听见。 没人说得清以哪份为准。 第三层是测试。 整套测试四十一项，其中九项测的就是这三份清单本身。 所以清单一旦改动，这九项会跟着动，看起来像在保质量，其实只是在保清单。 它建议的处理是：把这三份清单（大约三百行）连根删掉，回复一律交给模型判断，只留那条真正的安全规则，就是危险动作比如往正在跑的数据库迁移里发中断，仍然在代码层拦住不许过。 代价很实在，一句普通的「同意」会多等一秒左右，因为每次都要等模型想一下。 删表那条我还没替你回它，还在那儿等你点头。

transcript.text: What did bench-codex find about the flaky test? Explain it to me.

bench-codex found that the flaky test is not a real fault in your checkout. It passes most of the time, but on about one run in twelve the test starts before the discount prices have finished loading, so it calculates the full price instead of the member price and fails. That is what blocked two deploys last week, each needing a rerun. It changed nothing yet, and it offers two fixes: wait for the prices to load before starting the test, which is its recommendation, or swap in a fake price list just for that test. Shall I have it apply its recommended fix? Options: Apply the first fix, wait for the prices to load; Use a fake price list in that test instead; Leave it for now.
Then?

Nothing has moved since a moment ago. bench-codex finished its look and is idle, waiting to hear whether it should apply the fix. bench-claude is idle too and has not been given anything. Want me to have bench-codex apply its recommended fix? Options: Apply the first fix, wait for the prices to load; Use a fake price list in that test instead; Leave it for now.
More detail please.

Here is bench-codex's full finding. It ran that one test many times and it failed seven times out of eighty-four tries this week, roughly one run in twelve. The cause is a race at startup: the test sends its request before the discount prices have finished loading. When the test loses that race, the shop reads an empty price list and bills the plain price, so the total comes out a hundred instead of the eighty-five a member should pay. That is why the failure is random rather than constant. Shall I have bench-codex apply its recommended fix? Options: Apply the first fix, make the test wait for the prices; Use a stand-in price list in that test instead; Leave it for now.
Why does that happen?

It happens because two things start at the same moment and nothing makes them take turns. When the test runs, it fires off its request straight away, while the shop is still warming up and loading the discount prices in the background. If the request arrives before that loading finishes, the shop has no prices yet and falls back to the plain price, so the member discount is missing.
